chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When the soul reaches here – and he pointed with his hand to his throat – there will be no repentance for the scholar,
Then he recited: 'Verily repentance is upon Allah only for those who work evil in ignorance'
ai.seo_question: Why is repentance difficult for a scholar at the moment of sudden death?
ai.summary: The Imam states that for a scholar, if death occurs suddenly (indicated by the soul reaching the throat), there is no opportunity for repentance. He supports this by quoting the Quranic verse that repentance is for those who do evil in ignorance, implying that a scholar, possessing knowledge, cannot claim ignorance as an excuse for sudden death.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/44] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father AND Muhammad b. Ismail from al-Fadhl b. Shadhan all together from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil b. Darraj who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying: when the soul will reach here – and he pointed with his hand to his throat – there will be no repentance for the scholar
then he recited: “Verily repentance is upon Allāh only for those who work evil in ignorance” [4:17].
